guidance: # DOM-based reflected XSS via URLSearchParams hypothesis generation ## Phase alignment **Phase:** hypothesis_generation **Objective:** Form plausible hypotheses with known prerequisites, explicit assumptions and concrete future supporting or refuting checks. Unknown target conditions become future validation needs. No execution is performed. ## Scope definition ### Evidence present for hypothesis generation - Observation that client JavaScript reads `location.search` via `URLSearchParams`. - Observation that extracted value is written to a DOM sink. ### Evidence absent - Whether the specific parameter name is used. - Whether decoding, trimming or validation occurs before sink. - Whether the sink is HTML-parsing, script-evaluating or URL-context. - Whether browser URL-encoding of `location.search` neutralizes the payload. - Whether Content Security Policy or Trusted Types block execution. ## Hypothesis formulation template For each hypothesis document: 1. Hypothesis statement 2. Known technical prerequisites summary with status [Supported / Refuted / Unknown] 3. Prerequisite status table with Category; Status; Evidence; Future Check 4. Explicit assumptions checklist with Unverified tag, review date and rationale 5. Unknowns requiring future observation 6. Legitimate behavior vs boundary violation distinction 7. Baseline vs controlled variation and distinguishing evidence 8. Future supporting checks 9. Future refuting checks 10. Confidence rating with rationale ## Hypothesis 1: URLSearchParams → innerHTML HTML-parsing sink ### Hypothesis statement A query parameter read via `URLSearchParams` from `location.search` is assigned to `element.innerHTML` without sanitization, enabling DOM-based reflected XSS. ### Known prerequisites | Category | Status | Evidence | Future Check | |---|---|---|---| | Source readable via URLSearchParams | Unknown | Code pattern not confirmed | Search page JavaScript for `new URLSearchParams(location.search)` or `URLSearchParams` | | Parameter reflected to DOM | Unknown | No observation | Inject unique alphanumeric token and search DOM via DevTools | | Sink is innerHTML / insertAdjacentHTML / document.write | Unknown | No observation | Search JavaScript for assignments to `.innerHTML`, `.outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write` | | No client-side sanitization | Unknown | No observation | Trace data flow from URLSearchParams.get to sink for encode/escape | | Browser decodes location.search before URLSearchParams | Unknown | General behavior not confirmed for target | Confirm via console evaluation of `new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('p')` | | CSP / Trusted Types block | Unknown | No observation | Inspect response headers for `Content-Security-Policy` and `Trusted-Types` | ### Explicit assumptions - `URLSearchParams` is used on the page to parse `location.search`. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Required for source. - The sink is reached on initial page load without user interaction. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Needed for reflected trigger. - No Trusted Types policy is enforced for innerHTML. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Enforcement would block parser sink. ### Unknowns - Exact parameter name used. - Whether value is concatenated with other strings. - Whether the sink is created dynamically after load. ### Legitimate behavior vs boundary violation - Legitimate: Token appears as escaped text or is not rendered. - Boundary violation: Token creates executable DOM nodes, e.g., `marker` renders as bold element. ### Baseline vs controlled variation - Baseline: Load page with neutral query `?p=abc123`. Record DOM and network. - Variation: Load page with `?p=domx-test-7a4c` and inspect if token appears inside element rendered by innerHTML. - Distinguishing evidence: Token present in DOM tree but absent from raw HTTP response. ### Future supporting checks - Search all scripts for `URLSearchParams` and map `get` calls to variable names. - Use DevTools Sources `Ctrl+Shift+F` to find source variable usage and set breakpoint before sink assignment. - Inject unique token `domx-test-7a4c` and verify presence in DOM via `document.querySelectorAll('*')` text search. - If token found in innerHTML assignment, test with inert marker `domx-marker` and observe DOM creation, not execution. ### Future refuting checks - Confirm sink uses `textContent` instead of `innerHTML`. - Find sanitization library call between source and sink. - Observe that `URLSearchParams` value is only logged or sent to server. ### Confidence rating Low. Multiple Unknown prerequisites and no source confirmation yet. ## Hypothesis 2: URLSearchParams → document.write parser sink ### Hypothesis statement A query parameter extracted with `URLSearchParams` is passed to `document.write` or `document.writeln`, causing HTML parsing of attacker-controlled data. ### Known prerequisites | Category | Status | Evidence | Future Check | |---|---|---|---| | Source via URLSearchParams | Unknown | Pattern not confirmed | Static code search for `URLSearchParams` | | Sink is document.write | Unknown | No observation | Search scripts for `document.write` | | Write occurs during parsing phase | Unknown | Timing unknown | Check call stack location; document.write after load behaves differently | | No encoding applied | Unknown | No observation | Inspect code between extraction and write | | CSP blocks inline | Unknown | No observation | Check `Content-Security-Policy` for script-src restrictions | ### Explicit assumptions - `document.write` is executed synchronously during page load. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Timing affects parsing. - The written content includes the raw parameter value. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Needed for reflection. ### Unknowns - Whether surrounding context requires tag closure. - Whether write is conditional on parameter presence. ### Legitimate behavior vs boundary violation - Legitimate: Written content is static or escaped. - Boundary violation: Written content creates new DOM elements from parameter data. ### Future supporting checks - Locate `document.write` call and trace argument origin to `URLSearchParams.get`. - Inject token `domx-test-7a4c` and capture via DevTools console after load. - Review source for template literals concatenating parameter. ### Future refuting checks - `document.write` is used only for static assets. - Value is passed through `encodeURIComponent` before write. ### Confidence rating Low. Sink timing and encoding unknown. ## Hypothesis 3: URLSearchParams → JavaScript-evaluating sink ### Hypothesis statement A query parameter read via `URLSearchParams` is concatenated into a string passed to `eval`, `new Function`, `setTimeout(string)`, or similar JavaScript-evaluating sink. ### Known prerequisites | Category | Status | Evidence | Future Check | |---|---|---|---| | Source via URLSearchParams | Unknown | | Search for URLSearchParams usage | | Sink is eval-like | Unknown | | Search for `eval`, `Function`, `setTimeout` with string arg | | Data flow from source to sink | Unknown | | Debugger trace from get to sink | | CSP unsafe-eval allowed | Unknown | | Check CSP header for `unsafe-eval` | ### Explicit assumptions - String argument is not validated. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Validation would prevent execution. - Sink is reachable via crafted query. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Needed for trigger. ### Unknowns - Whether argument is wrapped in object property. - Whether CSP `unsafe-eval` is blocked. ### Legitimate behavior vs boundary violation - Legitimate: Parameter is used as data only. - Boundary violation: Parameter string is evaluated as code in browser. ### Future supporting checks - Set breakpoint on sink and inspect argument value with crafted query using inert marker. - Check CSP headers for `unsafe-eval`. ### Future refuting checks - Sink receives only static code. - Argument is passed as function reference, not string. ### Confidence rating Low. Eval sinks are common but confirmation needed. ## Hypothesis 4: URLSearchParams → attribute context sink ### Hypothesis statement Parameter value from `URLSearchParams` is written into an element attribute, e.g., `href`, `src`, `onerror`, enabling DOM-based XSS via attribute context. ### Known prerequisites | Category | Status | Evidence | Future Check | |---|---|---|---| | Source via URLSearchParams | Unknown | | Code search | | Attribute assignment via DOM property or setAttribute | Unknown | | Search for `.href =`, `.src =`, `setAttribute` | | No attribute encoding | Unknown | | Inspect assignment code | ### Explicit assumptions - Attribute is reflected verbatim. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Needed for breakout. - Browser will execute event handler attribute. [Unverified] Review date: TBD. Rationale: Needed for impact. ### Unknowns - Exact attribute name. - Whether value is URL-encoded. ### Legitimate behavior vs boundary violation - Legitimate: Attribute value is escaped or used as data. - Boundary violation: Attribute value changes element behavior, e.g., creates new element with different attribute. ### Future supporting checks - Inject token `domx-test-7a4c` and inspect attribute value in Elements panel. - Trace assignment from URLSearchParams.get to property set. ### Future refuting checks - Value is assigned to `textContent` only. - Attribute value is passed through `encodeURIComponent`. ### Confidence rating Low. Attribute context requires precise mapping. ## General future validation steps to establish unknown conditions 1. Source confirmation - Open page, run in console search for `URLSearchParams`. - Identify parameter name by inspecting `URLSearchParams` get calls. 2. Reflection confirmation - Choose unique token `domx-test-7a4c`. - Load `?p=domx-test-7a4c` and search DOM via DevTools `Ctrl+F` for token. - Compare raw HTTP response vs final DOM to confirm client-side reflection. 3. Sink identification - Use DevTools Sources search for sink names. - Set breakpoint on sink assignment and inspect variable provenance. 4. Encoding and sanitization check - Inject characters `< > " ' &`. - Observe if characters appear raw in DOM or are escaped. 5. Policy checks - Inspect response headers for `Content-Security-Policy` and `Trusted-Types`. - Note browser differences in URL-encoding of `location.search`. ## Controls and limitations - Do not execute active payloads without authorization. - Use harmless markers and inert content for future checks. - Preserve uncertainty until distinguishing evidence is collected. - Source coverage is limited to URLSearchParams read and parser sinks; other sources and sinks remain future checks.
